title: Mid-Range Bank Shot from the 45
description: Shooters catch on the move at the 45-degree spots just inside the three-point line and bank the jumper off the top corner of the square — a reliable angle shot for mid-range scorers.

content.objective: Use the backboard deliberately from the 45-degree angle at mid-range, catching on the move and aiming at the top corner.
content.setup: Passer at the top of the key; shooters start at the wing three-point line on each side.
content.organization: Shooter rebounds and passes to the passer line; alternate sides.
instructions: The shooter takes two steps in from the wing toward the 45-degree spot inside the arc.
Catch the pass on a 1-2 step with the shoulders turned to the board.
Aim at the top near corner of the square, not the rim.
Shoot with a slightly flatter arc than a straight-on shot so the ball meets the board on the way down.
coachingPoints: Pick the spot on the board before the catch.
Angle is everything: only bank from the 45.
Soft touch: the board absorbs speed.
commonMistakes: Banking from straight in front of the rim.
Hitting the middle of the square.
content.safety: Shooters rebound their own ball only when the lane is clear; nobody stands under the rim while others shoot.
variations: Bank shot off a curl cut.
Bank pull-up after a drive from the top.
successCriteria: Six of ten banked in from each side.
Ball hits the board inside the top corner.
content.gameApplication: Bank shots from the angle give mid-range scorers a bigger target than the rim.
